summary: Marianne Winder (1918–2001) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of London, University of Nottingham, University College London, and SOAS under David Llewellyn Snellgrove, later holding library and curatorial positions at Nottingham, London, and the Wellcome Trust.

Marianne Yaldiz worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and Direktorin at the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).
Marie G. Wanek worked in Indology and philosophy. She pursued her studies at the University of Pennsylvania under Sengaku Mayeda.
Marie-Stella Boussemart studied under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Marielle Harrison, a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, was a doctoral student at the University of Chicago and served as an HCBSS Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer at Stanford University (both attested 2026).

Marina Illich specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD in 2006 at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, also studying under Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Mario D'Amato (born 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He held posts at Hampshire College (~2001–2006) and Rollins College (~2007).

Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at UCLA in 2000 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he taught at the University of Iowa (2001) and the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).

Mario Praz (1896–1982) studied at the University of Bologna (~1915–1918) and the University of Florence (~1918–1920). He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, completing doctoral studies under supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, and studying under teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer (born 1954) is a historian and archaeologist. She held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (~1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (~2003–2020).

Marion Rastelli is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed her doctorate under Gerhard Oberhammer. She held positions at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and as a lecturer at the University of Vienna (attested 2020–2026).

Mark A. Nathan specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and later held posts at Kangwon National University, UCLA, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his doctorate at St John's College, Cambridge (~1989–1994) under K. R. Norman, and later held long-term posts at the University of Sydney, including department chair (attested 2015–2017) and associate professor.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi (born 1964) is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2007) and Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at the University of California, Berkeley (~2007).

Mark D. Griffiths (born 1966) studied at the University of Bradford (BSc, ~1984–1987) and the University of Exeter (PhD, 1988–1990). He held posts at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003), and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University (~2003).
Mark Hale is a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held posts attested at Harvard University in 1987 and Concordia University in 1997.

Mark I. Wallace (born 1956) earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1982–1986) under Paul Ricœur. Specializing in religious studies and philosophy, he taught at Merrimack College, Georgia State University, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Swarthmore College (~1989).

Mark Jan Dresden (1911–1986) studied Iranian and Central Asian languages and linguistics at Amsterdam and Utrecht, training under Jan Gonda, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Bruno Henning. He taught Iranian languages at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).
